title: The fixture oracle freezes this repo's live ledger, so adding a record fails it
foundBy: session agent, re-running viewer/fixtures after the @codesweep-ai/ui port
details:
`viewer/fixtures` runs every behavioural check against two corpora: this repository's own `ledger/`, and the frozen `fixtures/sandbox/ledger`. The `own` half records literal record ids and counts as frozen `keep` values. `ledger/` is the one corpus that grows. So a check that measures the viewer fails whenever the ledger it is pointed at changes.

Adding LGR-011 was enough. Seven checks failed, and none of them describes a viewer defect:

| check | what it froze |
|---|---|
| LF-02, LF-03, LF-04 | visible record set on own/board, own/list, own/activity |
| LF-12, LF-13 | the count behind `status - open` and `sev - crit` |
| LF-14 | a five-id sort order, `[LGR-001, LGR-009, LGR-010, LGR-008, LGR-007]` |
| LF-15 | the count `reset` returns to |

Every one has an exact twin against the sandbox corpus. Those twins are LF-06, LF-07, LF-08, LF-20, LF-21, LF-22 and LF-23, and all seven passed. The failures therefore left no behaviour unasserted.

Closing a record trips it as readily as adding one. LF-12 freezes the open and closed split, and LF-01 freezes the top of the queue as `[LGR-009, LGR-010]`. LF-01 passed only because LGR-011 did not surface in the brief view. About thirteen `own` checks are literal in this way, so six more are latent.

The cost is not the churn. Re-recording a `keep` row is gated on an approval id and a reason. `viewer/fixtures/README.md` reserves that for the case where a reviewer has agreed a behaviour genuinely changed. Spending the sign-off on a ledger that gained a record is how it becomes a rubber stamp. That disarms it for the change it exists to catch.

None of this is urgent. `make fixtures` sits outside `make check` and `make ci`, so nothing is red. The live-corpus value of `own` also survives, because its non-literal checks do not drift. LF-44 measures zero page errors and no external requests, and the axe, keyboard and size rows compare against thresholds.

There are two reasonable fixes. The first drops the literal-equality `own` variants that already have a frozen twin. That costs no behavioural coverage, but it gives up a second dataset shape, because sandbox renders three board lanes to own's two. Freezing a snapshot of `own` as a third corpus recovers it, which is what the sandbox corpus already is. The second makes the `own` variants relative, asserting invariants derived from the payload rather than frozen literals. That keeps the symmetry, at the cost of surgery on `run.mjs`.

notes.text: The latent set is not theoretical. LF-11, a search over `LGR-00`, drifted as soon as LGR-012 landed, so the approved re-record covered eight rows rather than seven. Appending this note moves the activity count in turn, which is the fault working as described.
